I'm assuming this isn't the name we want the port to have.
That's how it's been done in other configs.. Anyways, what else should i write here?
Maybe name the port the same way the NIC names it?

I'm not following.. What should i write down here?

Keep in mind i will also have to adjust it on the chassis side then as well, otherwise the association will not be created.
Maybe just "NicPort" or "MellanoxNicPort". There is no constraint on the `Name` property to contain the name of the association. `PortType` already expresses the association.

Thanks for the concrete suggestion, renamed it 👍

The `Name` property must match between 2 ports so i added the corresponding port on the chassis config as well.

> The Name property must match between 2 ports

?  This doesn't track for me.  2 ports shouldn't ever have the same name.  THis should be named whatever the silkscreen has it.  I don't have the part in front of me, so I can't tell you what you should write down, but you should look at what the port itself is labeled.  I'm pretty sure it's not labeled "GenericContainPort" on the PCB.
removed it since it's not a physical port and therefore not present on the silkscreen.
How does this work?  I don't think we have a PLDM backend for this that supports connectx?

This has nothing to do with PLDM.

It's an entity-manager feature to be able to create associations between the inventory items that it holds.

https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/docs/associations.md

In this case i am creating `contained_by` association here to the chassis. If you look into the chassis config you will find a port with the same name.

At runtime this enables creating the correct associations between inventory items.
Lets not call sensors "Ignore".
Renamed to `NIC Temp 1 $bus`
Did we get the correct type here?  If these don't use a TMP421, lets figure out the right device.

I took a look at the card again from all sides and also looked into the document you found 
https://docs.nvidia.com/nvidia-connectx-6-ethernet-adapter-cards-user-manual.pdf


The document states

> The adapter card incorporates the ConnectX IC, which operates in the range of temperatures
between 0°C and 105°C.

and

> The card's thermal sensors can be read through the system’s SMBus. The user can read these
thermal sensors and adapt the system airflow following the readouts and the needs of the above-
mentioned IC thermal

I assume that the temperature sensor is directly part of the SoC and not a separate chip. So there is no way for me to figure which one it is supposed to be or if it even models an existing temp sensor on I2C or some custom solution.

I don't see any way i can make progress here on my own, even if i tried all possible drivers for i2c temp sensors, it would not tell us anything about what's really in there.

The options i see currently:

- you confirm internally within nvidia what's the correct driver to use
- we go with the current version, accepting that there's a dead temp channel until someone fixes the config
- we drop the temp sensor from the config, leaving users with an inventory item but no temperature reading (IMO the worst options since these NICs tend to run pretty hot)

> lets figure out the right device.

@ed@tanous.net @molberding@nvidia.com can you help with finding the information ?

From what i can tell based on public information, i have no clue about this temp sensor. I can try different drivers but that only tells us what it isn't.

As written, yes the type of sensor is not entirely clear. But the driver works and the temperature reading is **real and useful**.

So i would consider the patch an improvement and if anyone knows it better they can always adjust this config 😊

> I assume that the temperature sensor is directly part of the SoC and not a separate chip.

Exactly, so a TMP421 device in your EM config isn't appropriate here unless you actually have a TMP421.  If you want to invent a new device called "connectx6 temp sensor" that's fine, but please don't put in configs that we know to be incorrect.

> i have no clue about this temp sensor. 

That's fine, then go create a new device type for this sensor and how it behaves.

> Exactly, so a TMP421 device in your EM config isn't appropriate here unless you actually have a TMP421.

> That's fine, then go create a new device type for this sensor and how it behaves.

No, this is not what we should be doing.

What you are asking for requires Alexander to write a kernel driver with the new type.  But he doesn't have information to even formulate a successful commit message to the kernel let alone a whole new driver.

The types here are effectively "compatible" names; they are not literal device names.  There are other examples already in the EM tree where the "real" device isn't the literal stamped name of the device in a chip either.  But, if it acts like a TMP421, talks like a TMP421, we label it as a TMP421.  This is honestly the same behavior in the kernel and QEMU as well.

TMP421 is a 20+ year old i2c design.  The CX-6 has been GA for over 6 years old.  These things aren't changing.  Asking the kernel to add a new compatible string just to be "more explicit" here isn't worth the effort it would take to make it happen.

> What you are asking for requires Alexander to write a kernel driver with the new type. 

This is not what I asked for, and i agree, a new kernel driver for this would be overkill assuming the one leg of TMP421 works.

We should add a new type that can use the TMP421 in the kernel, and just ignore one leg of it so we don't get errant readings.  Should just be a hwmontempsensor change to come up with a way to ignore the one leg of the TMP421 that isn't working.

Exposing a broken temp sensor that we know can't ever read doesn't seem right, and would be an openbmc bug for any system that has this card in it.

hwmontempsensor has had support in for a few years now to only read the sensors based on what's in "Labels", https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/commit/9eb0cc3d8272bcdc58ead70c9a39fe8cecd5b6b5, so there is no case here of garbage readings (unless I'm missing something).
The problem here is that the label will exist in hwmon, the sensor will just give incorrect readings (because the part isn't actually tmp421 compatible).

oh, I see, I wasn't aware that was even a feature.

Lets get the "best effort" part out of the commit message, get a tested statement that includes reading the temp values, then we're good to go.
Done

This could match both the dual port variant of the card and the single port variant of the card.  Presumably (especially if we're enumerating the port above) we need two configs.

Either:
Remove the port definition so this is correct for both variants
Duplicate the config for the two variants, making this regex more specific.= to the single port variant.
The `"Type": "Port"` config record has nothing to do with physical network ports, it is used to create associations.

which i believe are quite similar as they also have a `TMP421` with unused channel.
is this the right size part, or did you just pick the largest?  The docs I could find didn't specify the size here.  It's fine as is, but if we know the size, lets pick the right part.

I don't know the size but looked again at the part. Did not spot the eeprom on there, either it is too small to see it properly or it is emulated by the SoC.

Someone can always adjust it later if they have more information.

This is similar to https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/configurations/nvidia/cx7_mezzanine_module.json
and https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/configurations/nvidia/cx8_mezzanine_module.json

with regards to `Labels, Name, Name1`

and should work the same with regards to the unused channel.

They ignore it as well so it seems to be a similar situation like the configs which are already in tree.

Remove this statement and replace it with a Tested statement please.  The disclaimer is already covered by the license at the root of the repo.

Ideally in your tested check that:
1. Only one temp sensor is exposed.
2. That temp sensor appears to have a reasonable value.

After that, this patch should be good to go.
